text:
[LREG.8.3] **The admitted surface is RE2's, entire.** [LREG.8.1] admits
no superset and no subset, so every construct RE2 accepts is writable in
a DS pattern. No list of them is kept here: a hand-maintained copy of
another specification's grammar drifts, nothing checks it, and this one
had ([STYL.2.15.1]).

What follows is not an enumeration but the residue — the places where a
pattern that looks right to an author coming from another engine is not
RE2:

- The Unicode escape is `\x{10FFFF}`. The `\u{HHHH}` form is JavaScript
  and Rust notation; RE2 has never had it.
- The absolute anchors are `\A` and `\z`. `\Z` is not RE2.
- `(?U)` **inverts the greediness of every quantifier after it** for the
  remainder of the pattern. It is admitted, and it is the one flag that
  changes what a pattern matches rather than how it is read — note that
  it arrives inside the pattern body, not in the literal's flag position
  ([LREG.5]).
- `(?<name>...)` and `(?P<name>...)` both name a group and reach the
  same capture; [LREG.3] writes the first.
- Unicode classes (`\pL`, `\p{Greek}`) and POSIX classes
  (`[[:alpha:]]`) are admitted, on the same grounds as everything else
  RE2 accepts.
